hints: Look first at the central alpha carbon in each diagram and spot its four standard attachments: H, the amino group, the carboxyl group, and the side chain.
Remember the R group is everything attached to the alpha carbon except H, NH3+ / NH2+, and COO-, and for proline on the right the ring loops back so only the three CH2 groups count as R.
walkthrough:
**Recall what counts as the R group**

Every amino acid has the same backbone. The central alpha carbon is joined to H, to the amino group, to the carboxyl group, and to the R group.

So the rule is simple:
$$R = \text{side chain only, not backbone}$$

**Check the left amino acid, histidine**

The left structure has $H_3N^+$ on the left, $COO^-$ on the right, and H on top of the alpha carbon. Everything hanging down from the alpha carbon is the imidazole ring side chain.

The correct highlight must cover only that ring side chain and must leave the alpha carbon, amino group and carboxyl group white.

**Check the right amino acid, proline**

Proline is special because its side chain loops back to join its own nitrogen to make a ring. The alpha carbon is joined to H on top, $COO^-$ on the right, $H_2N^+$ on the left, and $CH_2$ below.

The R group is only the chain of three $CH_2$ groups: $CH_2-CH_2-CH_2$. It does not include the nitrogen, the alpha carbon, or the carboxyl group.

**Pick the pair that highlights only R in both**

Only option D leaves all backbone groups white in both diagrams and shades just the histidine ring on the left and just the three $CH_2$ groups on the right. That matches the definition perfectly.

options.A: Left diagram wrongly shades the carboxyl group as well as R, and right diagram wrongly includes the alpha carbon in the shading.
options.B: Both diagrams shade the backbone amino and carboxyl groups, which are never part of the R group.
options.C: Left diagram includes the alpha carbon in the shading, and right diagram includes the amino nitrogen, so neither shows R only.
options.D: Left shades only the histidine ring side chain and right shades only the three CH2 groups of proline, leaving backbone H, amino and carboxyl groups unshaded.
